title: One accuracy score can hide problems

sections.skill: Explain why one accuracy score can hide problems and plan inclusive testing

questions.prompt: In this prepared example, what is the overall accuracy?
questions.intro: One overall ACCURACY score can hide serious problems. If a tool is 95% accurate overall, it might be 98% accurate for a large group and only 70% for a small one, because the large group dominates the average. It can also hide poor results on rare but important CASES, such as unusual accents or uncommon medical conditions. INCLUSIVE TESTING breaks results down: by group, by situation and by type of case. It includes enough examples from smaller groups to measure them reliably, and checks the cases where errors would cause the most harm.

sections.skill: Compare an overall score with a class average

questions.prompt: What does the 85% average hide?

choices.text: That every student in the class scored exactly eighty-five percent on the test

questions.intro: A class average of 85% on a test sounds good. But if 25 students scored about 90% and 3 students scored about 40%, the average hides that those 3 students are struggling. A teacher who only looks at the average would miss them. Tool accuracy works the same way: the overall number can look fine while one group or type of case is failing.

questions.prompt: Why does the average still look good?

choices.text: Because the low scores were not counted, since only high scores go into an average

sections.skill: Handle the practical side of inclusive testing

questions.prompt: With 10 examples in a group, how much does one error move the rate?
questions.intro: Breaking results down raises practical questions. Small groups give noisy numbers: with 10 examples, one error moves the rate by 10 points, so collect more where possible. Some group information is sensitive and must be gathered with consent and care. And deciding which groups and cases to test is itself a choice; involving the people affected helps reveal cases a team would not think of.
